correctness.rationale: All ternary necklaces through length 6 are exhaustively generated and checked against the necklace-count formula. Two independent circular-Parikh computations agree on every object. At length 5 the unique nontrivial full-support M-class is CE-connected. At length 6 exactly eight nontrivial full-support M-classes occur; two independently constructed CE edge sets agree, with five connected classes and exactly three disconnected classes of sizes 2,2,3. Every one of the seven exceptional words has no CE1 or CE2 move.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies incompleteness of CE1 and CE2 as a limitation and asks for stronger rules. Locating the first full-support failure and classifying the entire minimal equality layer directly sharpens that open structural issue. The result distinguishes one completely explained length-5 ambiguity from exactly three genuinely unexplained length-6 classes, making the finite boundary useful for designing any future complete rule system.
